title: RuleSmith: Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Game Balancing
claim: A closed loop where LLM agents self-play under a rulebook and an optimizer tunes the rules until the game is balanced.
layout: Single illustrated scene; agents and board left, optimizer top-right, rulebook bottom-right, glowing flow arcs
description: A parchment-style illustration, drawn as a single scene. Two translucent blue humanoid figures labeled LLM Agent A and LLM Agent B lean over a hex-grid game board and move miniature pieces. The label 'Self-play' sits between them. In the foreground a brass balance scale holds a stone castle labeled Empire on one pan and horse-riding nomads with tents labeled Nomads on the other. A central dial between the pans reads 'Balanced, 50% win rate'. At the top right, a compass-and-gear mechanism labeled 'Bayesian Optimization Engine' includes a small probability-curve plot. At the bottom right, an open rulebook has green and red bars for Unit Health, Production Cost and Damage for each faction. Glowing golden streams run from the rulebook up to the optimizer. The 'RULESMITH' title plaque sits at the bottom center. The eye goes first to the scale and the game board.
caption: Overview of RuleSmith. RuleSmith treats asymmetric game balancing as optimization over game rollouts using multi-agent LLMs given a natural-language rulebook. It optimizes interpretable parameters such as unit HP, attack damage, resource gain, production cost, and scoring weights. For each candidate game parameter setting, two LLM agents play the game zero-shot, and their outcomes estimate the faction win rates and balance loss. A Bayesian optimizer then proposes new settings, while adaptive sampling allocates more games to promising candidates. This enables closed-loop balancing without task-specific policy training, reducing manual playtesting and parameter tuning. Figure generated by Nano Banana Pro.
abstract: Game balancing is a longstanding challenge requiring repeated playtesting, expert intuition, and extensive manual tuning. We introduce RuleSmith, a framework that couples multi-agent LLM self-play with surrogate-based optimization over a parameterized rule space. As a proof of concept, we build CivMini, a simplified civilization-style game with two asymmetric factions governed by 12 tunable parameters. LLM agents interpret textual rulebooks and game states to propose actions that are validated by the game engine, yielding noisy estimates of faction win rates. Our primary implementation uses Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization with Expected-Improvement-based adaptive sampling to allocate more evaluation games to promising candidates. RuleSmith consistently finds near-balanced configurations: three independent optimization runs reach near-even empirical win rates in independent 200- and 300-game evaluations, and additional experiments with NTBEA and TPE show that the same self-play interface supports different search components. Cross-model evaluations and small human studies provide preliminary evidence of transfer across player populations. RuleSmith produces interpretable numerical rule adjustments without task-specific policy training. Project and code: https://adonis-galaxy.github.io/RuleSmith-website/
